title: Face-localized toric chart strata and unit-compatible completed sharp charts
statement:
Let $(W,M_W)$ be a locally Noetherian fs log regular scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], with a global fs chart $R\to M_W$ and structural map $\alpha:R\to\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$. Let $Q$ be fs and $h:R\to Q$ any monoid homomorphism. Define
$$Z=W\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[R]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]$$
using the ordinary scheme fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], endowed with its associated $Q$-chart log structure. Monoid rings have basis $[q]$ and multiplication $[q][q']=[q+q']$. Choose a geometric point $\bar z:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Z$, put $\bar w=\operatorname{pr}_W\bar z$ [def-weil-geometric-point], and let $A=\mathcal O^{\rm sh}_{W,\bar w}$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Lift $\bar z$ to $Z_A=\operatorname{Spec}A\times_W Z$ using the closed geometric point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and the same $\Omega$. Let $\mathfrak q$ be the underlying prime in $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[R]}\mathbf Z[Q]$, and put $B=(A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[R]}\mathbf Z[Q])_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then $Z$ and $Z_A$ are locally Noetherian, $A,B$ are nonzero Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $A\to B$ is local, and $\mathfrak q$ contracts to $\mathfrak m$.
Put $F=\{q\in Q:[q]\in B^\times\}$ and $G=\{r\in R:\alpha(r)\in A^\times\}$. Then $F,G$ are faces and $h^{-1}(F)=G$. Write $R_G=\{r-g:r\in R,g\in G\}$ and $Q_F=\{q-f:q\in Q,f\in F\}$ inside the respective group completions, and $S=R_G/G^{\rm gp}$, $T=Q_F/F^{\rm gp}$. These are sharp fs monoids with finite free group completions, and are respectively the characteristic monoids at $\bar w$ and at the lifted geometric point of $Z_A$. Put $I=(\alpha(r):r\notin G)A$ and $J=([q]:q\notin F)B$. These are the corresponding nonunit log ideals; the characteristics stay $S,T$ on the strict localizations. For the induced prime $\mathfrak p$ there is a canonical isomorphism
$$B/J\cong\left((A/I)\otimes_{\mathbf Z[G^{\rm gp}]}\mathbf Z[F^{\rm gp}]\right)_{\mathfrak p},$$
where $[g]$ acts as $\alpha(g)$ on $A/I$ and as $[h(g)]$ on the other factor.
Moreover there exist a sharp chart $a:S\to A$ inducing the indicated characteristic identification and a character $\epsilon:R^{\rm gp}\to A^\times$ such that $\alpha(r)=\epsilon(r)a(\bar r)$ for all $r\in R_G$, with $\alpha$ extended by inverting $G$. For some finite $n\ge0$, compatibly with $a(s)$, the completion $\widehat A$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is $k[[S]][[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ in equal characteristic, or $V[[S]][[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]/(\theta)$ in mixed characteristic $(0,p)$. Here $k=A/\mathfrak m$, $V$ is a Cohen ring with residue field $k$ and uniformizer $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring], and $\theta-p\in([s]:s\ne0,t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. For a local coefficient ring $E$, the notation $E[[S]][[t]]$ denotes the completion of $E[S][t]$ at $(\mathfrak m_E,[s]:s\ne0,t_1,\ldots,t_n)$.

source.place: VI 1.6, p.70, and VIII 3.1.1--3.1.5, pp.98--99; face stratum and unit-twisted sharp-chart preparation from returned item steps 4--5 (agent-supplied refinements of the displayed local models).

proof.text: Work on an affine chart neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}D$ of the image $w$ of $\bar w$, chosen from a Noetherian affine cover of $W$, and let $\mathfrak p_w\subset D$ be the prime of $w$. By the etale-local-ring/triple comparison, the affine pointed neighbourhoods of $\bar w$ factoring through $U$ are initial and correspond to the triples over $(D,\mathfrak p_w)$ with values in the separable closure of $\kappa(w)$ in $\Omega$; hence $A$ is canonically the triple colimit of the strict-henselization triple theorem, which is the strict henselization $(D_{\mathfrak p_w})^{\rm sh}$, a local ring whose maximal ideal is the kernel of the closed geometric-point evaluation. Localization preserves Noetherianity, so $D_{\mathfrak p_w}$ is a Noetherian local ring, and so does strict henselization; thus $A$ is Noetherian. Apply toric-chart fs realization to $D,R,Q,h$ on each such $U$, and to $A,R,Q,h$: it gives Noetherian chart rings and their associated fs log structures. The affine fibre-product identification makes these precisely the inverse images of $U$ in $Z$, and $Z_A=\operatorname{Spec}C$, where $C=A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[R]}\mathbf Z[Q]$. Hence $Z,Z_A$ are locally Noetherian. Finally $B=C_{\mathfrak q}$ is Noetherian by localization.

source.place: VI 1.1; Noetherian bookkeeping in chart realizations; Stacks 04HX (pointed etale neighbourhoods vs triples), 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 06LJ (lemma-henselization-noetherian).

proof.text: The evaluation $A\to\Omega$ at the closed geometric point, paired with the given $\bar z$, defines its lift to the fibre product. Its kernel on $A$ is $\mathfrak m$, so the prime $\mathfrak q=\ker(C\to\Omega)$ contracts to $\mathfrak m$. The strict-henselization local structure makes $A$ local, and prime localization makes $B$ local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak qB$. Thus the preimage of this maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m$, proving that $A\to B$ is local. Both rings are nonzero: they admit the displayed unital maps to the field $\Omega$. In a local homomorphism an element is a unit exactly when its image is: a nonunit belongs to the maximal ideal and its image does too.

source.place: VI 1.2 (strict-local setup); Stacks 04GP and 04GW (closed point of strict henselization).

proof.text: For any homomorphism to a commutative ring, the inverse image of the units is a face: if $xy$ is a unit, $y(xy)^{-1}$ and $x(xy)^{-1}$ are inverses for $x$ and $y$. This proves the face assertions. Since $[h(r)]=\alpha(r)$ in $B$, reflection of units in step 2 proves $h^{-1}(F)=G$. Apply fs face sharpening separately to $(R,G)$ and $(Q,F)$: it gives exactly $S,T$, their sharp fs structure and finite free group completions. Apply the characteristic comparison for a fixed global chart to $W$ and $Z_A$. At their selected points the ordinary local unit faces are $G$ and $F$, respectively: $B$ is the local ring of $Z_A$ at the image of the lifted point, and for $W$ the map $\mathcal O_{W,w}=D_{\mathfrak p_w}\to A$ is local (step 1: the maximal ideal of $A$ is the kernel of the evaluation at $\bar w$, whose contraction to $D$ is $\mathfrak p_w$), so by the unit criterion of step 2 an $\alpha(r)$ is a unit in $\mathcal O_{W,w}$ exactly when it is a unit in $A$; and its geometric-stalk comparison identifies the characteristics with $S,T$. The same stalks describe the closed points of the strict localizations, so these characteristic identifications persist there. The chart pushout shows that every log nonunit is a unit times a chart element outside its unit face; consequently its structural images generate precisely $I$ and $J$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.1--3.1.5; VI 1.1--1.2 (chart pushout, characteristics and nonunit ideal).

proof.text:
Here is the stratum calculation directly on generators. Invert $[f]$ for all $f\in F$ in $C$; call the result $C_F$. Write $K$ for its ideal generated by $[q]$ with $q
otin F$. Since $F$ is a face, a sum with a summand outside $F$ remains outside $F$. Therefore the assignment sending $[q]$ to $0$ for $q
otin F$ and sending $[f]$ to its group monomial for $f\in F$ is multiplicative. Put $D'=(A/I)\otimes_{\mathbf Z[G^{m gp}]}\mathbf Z[F^{m gp}]$. Define $C_F	o D'$ by $a\mapsto ar a\otimes1$, $[q]\mapsto0$ outside $F$, and $[f]\mapsto1\otimes[f]$ on $F$. Tensor balancing holds: for $r
otin G$ both $\alpha(r)$ and $[h(r)]$ map to zero; for $r\in G$ it is exactly balancing over $\mathbf Z[G^{m gp}]$. This kills $K$. Conversely $A	o C_F/K$ kills $I$, since $r
otin G$ implies $h(r)
otin F$; the invertible monomials of $F$ define $\mathbf Z[F^{m gp}]	o C_F/K$. The same balancing gives $D'	o C_F/K$. These maps are inverse on coefficients and on all monomials, which generate the rings. Localizing this isomorphism at the prime induced by $\mathfrak q$ yields the stated $B/J\cong D'_{\mathfrak p}$. Indeed $K$ lies in that prime since its generators are nonunits in $B$, and passage to the local quotient sends a fraction $c/d$ to $ ar c/ ar d$; its inverse is the same fraction rule. Thus quotient and this localization agree without any flatness assertion.

source.place: VIII 3.1.1--3.1.5; agent expansion of the face-stratum computation in the item source.

proof.text: Choose a sharp chart of $W$ at $\bar w$ by the sharp-chart lemma, using the characteristic identification $S$ from step 3. Apply the completed-chart lemma and keep the possibly replaced sharp chart $a_M:S\to M_{W,\bar w}$, with structural map $a:S\to A$, that it supplies. Its complete-local-ring presentations are exactly those requested: its notation $B_k(S,n)$ and $B_V(S,n)$ means completion of the displayed monoid polynomial ring at the displayed maximal ideal. It gives the same monomial compatibility and the same congruence for $\theta$. No completed presentation for the initial, unreplaced chart is being assumed.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p.70 (choose the chart giving the complete local model).

proof.text: It remains to relate that particular chart to the original $R$ chart. The localized chart pushout identifies the log stalk with $R_G\oplus_{G^{\rm gp}}A^\times$. Since $S^{\rm gp}$ is finite free, integral-monoid sharpening splitting gives a section $s:S\to R_G$ and $R_G\simeq S\oplus G^{\rm gp}$. Its pushout is $S\oplus A^\times$, hence integral. The split-coordinate lemma therefore applies to this log stalk and the selected $a_M$ (both induce the same identification of $S$). It supplies a homomorphism $u:S\to A^\times$ such that the original log chart at $s(v)$ equals $a_M(v)$ times $u(v)$. Extend $u$ uniquely to $S^{\rm gp}$ by $u(v-v')=u(v)u(v')^{-1}$. For $r\in R_G$, write $v=\bar r$ and $g=r-s(v)\in G^{\rm gp}$, and set $\epsilon(r)=u(v)\alpha(g)$. Both $r\mapsto v$ and $r\mapsto g$ are additive, so this is a homomorphism into units. It extends to $R^{\rm gp}=R_G^{\rm gp}$ by the group-completion relations. Applying the structural map to the log-stalk equality gives $\alpha(r)=\epsilon(r)a(\bar r)$ on $R_G$. The cancellation here takes place in the integral log stalk, never by dividing structural monomials in $A$, which might be zero.
